status_summary: The administration has proposed cuts and consolidation and House committees have moved toward lower DOL spending and WIOA changes, but Congress has enacted none of it: the FY 2027 request would cut DOL discretionary spending to $9.9 billion from $13.3 billion and replace many WIOA Title I programs with a block grant, and the House Appropriations Committee advanced a FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34-28 on 2026-06-09 that, per the National Association of Workforce Boards, funds DOL at $9.8 billion, while H.R. 8210, a WIOA reauthorization, cleared the House Education and Workforce Committee 19-14 on 2026-04-21. EO 14278 (signed 2025-04-23) ordered a review of federal workforce programs that could recommend consolidating or eliminating programs. DOL's 2025-05-29 pause of contractor-operated Job Corps centers was preliminarily enjoined in New York on 2025-06-25, and in a settlement filed 2026-08-10 in Cabrera v. Department of Labor (D.D.C.) DOL agreed to rescind the pause and termination notices. Public Law 119-103, signed 2026-09-02, continues FY 2026 Labor-HHS-Education funding through 2026-12-11, so full-year FY 2027 decisions remain open.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14278 (published 2025-04-28). Section 3 directs the Secretaries of Labor, Commerce and Education to review federal workforce programs within 90 days and recommend integrating systems, reforming or eliminating ineffective programs, and consolidating programs.

DOL announces it will begin shutting down contractor-operated Job Corps centers; EPI ties the move to a White House budget request that would eliminate Job Corps and cut DOL's workforce training budget by more than half in favor of a proposed state and local grant program.

After a temporary restraining order on 2025-06-04, a federal judge in the Southern District of New York (Judge Andrew Carter, per VTDigger) issues a preliminary injunction that keeps Job Corps centers open while litigation continues, finding DOL likely lacked authority to end a congressionally mandated program.

House Education and Workforce Chair Tim Walberg introduces the A Stronger Workforce for America Act of 2026 (H.R. 8210), a WIOA reauthorization with a 50 percent training requirement, expanded performance reporting and consolidation waivers for up to 10 states; the committee approves it 19-14 on 2026-04-21 and it awaits House floor action.

The administration's initial FY 2027 request (as summarized by the National Association of Workforce Boards) would cut DOL discretionary spending to $9.9 billion from $13.3 billion in FY 2026, create a Make America Skilled Again block grant combining WIOA Title I programs, eliminate Job Corps and eliminate the Senior Community Service Employment Program; DOL's budget page lists FY 2027 budget documents.

Bloomberg Government reports (month only; the first of the month is used) that a House Appropriations package rejects the $3.4 billion Make America Skilled Again framework for the second year in a row, cuts Job Corps by almost $1 billion instead of eliminating it, allocates $5 million to registered apprenticeships, and closes OFCCP, the Women's Bureau and the Bureau of International Labor Affairs.

The full House Appropriations Committee advances its FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34-28; per NAWB, the subcommittee draft cuts DOL to $9.8 billion (27 percent), reduces WIOA Title I formula grants 62 percent and eliminates Youth, and the full committee left core WIOA funding levels unchanged.

The House passes a continuing resolution (H.R. 9770) extending FY 2026 funding through December 11; the Senate was advancing a similar measure, and full-year FY 2027 decisions were expected in late fall (per NAWB).

In Cabrera v. Department of Labor (D.D.C., No. 25-1909), DOL and student plaintiffs file a stipulated settlement and dismissal under which DOL is to rescind its 2025-05-29 Job Corps pause and related termination notices and take no further action on them, with the case to be dismissed with prejudice after entry.

timeline.event: The President signs H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (Public Law 119-103), funding agencies through 2026-12-11; the Senate passed it 90-6 on 2026-08-08 (vote 228) and the House concurred in the Senate amendments 370-48 on 2026-09-01.
